Additional Information

questions.question: Directions: Select the correct direct form of the given sentence. She said that she had met an old friend the day before.

Directions: Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is She said, “I met an old friend yesterday.”

Key Points

  • The given sentence is an indirect speech.
  • The basic rules for changing or converting indirect speech into direct speech:​
    • The commas and inverted commas are added and 'that' is removed.
    • The third-person pronoun 'she' is changed to the first-person pronoun 'I' and the phrase "the day before'' becomes ''yesterday''.
    • The past perfect tense format 'Subject + had + V3 (met) + Object' will be changed into the past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (met) + Object'.
       

Hence, the correct sentence is option 4.

Additional Information

  • The following table will enable us to know how tense changes:
     
    Direct Speech Indirect Speech
    Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object) Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
    Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object) Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past simple (Subject+V2+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object) Past perfect continuous (Subject +had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object) Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object)
    Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object) Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

Choose the option that is the correct direct form of the sentence.

He said that he had taken French lessons on Duolingo.

options.text: He said, “I have taken French lessons on Duolingo.”
options.html: He said, “I have taken French lessons on Duolingo.”

options.text: He said, “You took French lessons on Duolingo. “
options.html: He said, “You took French lessons on Duolingo. “

options.text: He says, “He has taken French lessons on Duolingo.”
options.html: He says, “He has taken French lessons on Duolingo.”

options.text: He said, “I take French lessons on Duolingo.”
options.html: He said, “I take French lessons on Duolingo.”

questions.solution: While changing the sentence from indirect to direct speech, commas and inverted commas will be added. Past perfect tense will change into present perfect tense, and "he" will be changed into "I". Therefore, the correct sentence is "He said, 'I have taken French lessons on Duolingo'".

questions.question: Directions: Select the option that is the direct form of the sentence. Kirti asked me if I had watched the movie on television the previous night.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the option that is the direct form of the sentence.

Kirti asked me if I had watched the movie on television the previous night.

options.text: Kirti asked me, “Did you watch the movie on television last night ?”
options.html: Kirti asked me, “Did you watch the movie on television last night ?”

options.text: Kirti asked me, “Had you watched the movie on television last night ?”
options.html: Kirti asked me, “Had you watched the movie on television last night ?”

options.text: Kirti asked me, “You had watched the movie on television last night ?”
options.html: Kirti asked me, “You had watched the movie on television last night ?”

options.text: Kirti asked me, “Did I watched the movie on television last night ?”
options.html: Kirti asked me, “Did I watched the movie on television last night ?”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- Kirti asked me, “Did you watch the movie on television last night ?” 

Key Points​

  • Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from indirect to direct speech:
  • The tense of direct speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
  • When the indirect speech is in an assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
    • Connectors 'whether/why' or 'if' are replaced by the comma and inverted commas.
    • The tense of reported speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense. 
    • Change the reported speech from assertive to interrogative.
    • The personal pronouns will be changed according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
    • ​Here the 1st person 'I' will change into the 2nd person 'you' as per the object.
    • Past perfect tense (had watched) in indirect speech changes to Past simple in direct speech (Did you watch).
    • Words showing time and place are changed accordingly. (the previous night-last night)
  • ​At last line up the remaining part.
     

 Following these steps, we finally get- Kirti asked me, “Did you watch the movie on television last night ?”

questions.question: Select the correct direct form of the given sentence. The surgeon says that I should get anaesthesia for the surgery.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
The surgeon says that I should get anaesthesia for the surgery.

options.text: The surgeon says, “You should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”
options.html: The surgeon says, “You should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”

options.text: The surgeon says, “I should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”
options.html: The surgeon says, “I should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”

options.text: The surgeon said, “You should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”
options.html: The surgeon said, “You should get anaesthesia for the surgery.”

options.text: The surgeon says, “You could get anaesthesia for the surgery.”
options.html: The surgeon says, “You could get anaesthesia for the surgery.”

questions.solution: While changing to direct speech, inverted commas and a conjunction will be used. The first word of direct speech is capitalized, and the tense remains the same as the reporting verb is in the present tense. The 1st person pronoun "I" is changed to the 2nd person pronoun "you" in direct speech.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. He asked me when I had booked the flight tickets.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He asked me when I had booked the flight tickets.

options.text: He said to me, “When did you book the flight tickets?”
options.html: He said to me, “When did you book the flight tickets?”

options.text: He said to me, “When are you booking the flight tickets?”
options.html: He said to me, “When are you booking the flight tickets?”

options.text: He said to me, “When do you book the flight tickets?”
options.html: He said to me, “When do you book the flight tickets?”

options.text: He said to me, “When you had book the flight tickets?”
options.html: He said to me, “When you had book the flight tickets?”

questions.solution: The correct answer is: He said to me, “When did you book the flight tickets?” The Past Perfect tense ('had booked') in indirect speech changes back to the Simple Past tense ('did book') in direct speech, and the pronoun 'I' changes to 'you'.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. The guard told the children to stay away from the flower beds.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The guard told the children to stay away from the flower beds.

options.text: The guard said, “Children, should you stay away from the flower beds.”
options.html: The guard said, “Children, should you stay away from the flower beds.”

options.text: The guard said, “Children, stay away from the flower beds.”
options.html: The guard said, “Children, stay away from the flower beds.”

options.text: The guard told to the children, “ Stay away from the flower beds.”
options.html: The guard told to the children, “ Stay away from the flower beds.”

options.text: The guard says to the children, “ Stay away from the flower beds.”
options.html: The guard says to the children, “ Stay away from the flower beds.”

questions.solution: In the given sentence, the reporting verb "told" changes to "said" in direct speech as this is a first-person narrative. As the guard is saying the sentence to the children., there should be a comma after children to put emphasis on them within the inverted commas.

questions.question: Select the correct direct form of the given sentence. My teacher forbids to trust one’s relatives.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

My teacher forbids to trust one’s relatives.

options.text: My teacher says, “Never trust your relatives.”
options.html: My teacher says, “Never trust your relatives.”

options.text: My teacher says, “Never trust my relatives.”
options.html: My teacher says, “Never trust my relatives.”

options.text: My teacher says, “Never trusted your relatives.”
options.html: My teacher says, “Never trusted your relatives.”

options.text: My teacher said “Never trust your relatives.”
options.html: My teacher said “Never trust your relatives.”

questions.solution: In direct speech, the tense remains the same if the reporting verb is in the present tense. "One's" is changed to "your" as per the object of the reporting verb. Commas and inverted commas are added, and the connector "to" is removed. Reported speech 'says' will be added. 'forbids to trust' will be changed to 'never trust'.
